patches.entity_key: Past conditional for unconfirmed past information (journalistic)
value: Not used for verified factual reporting, which takes the indicative
Typically third-person, reporting what others are said to have done

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated trap; the third-person tendency is standard journalistic usage.

patches.entity_key: Past conditional with si clause in plus-que-parfait
value: The past conditional never appears in the si clause
For present or future hypotheses, si + imparfait with the present conditional is used instead

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated condition and trap; the present-hypothesis counterpart is standard grammar.

value: Agreement with the subject occurs only with être, not with avoir
The auxiliary is never conjugated; it stays in the infinitive

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated agreement rule; the second follows from the formation.

value: When the main clause is in the present, the future is kept in the dependent clause
The conditionnel here marks a tense shift, not a hypothesis

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated condition; the second distinguishes this use from conditional sentences.

patches.entity_key: Past main clause: passé composé → plus-que-parfait
value: When the main clause is in the present, the passé composé is kept in the dependent clause
The plus-que-parfait marks anteriority relative to the past main clause

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated condition; the second follows from the tense-concordance rule.

value: When the main clause is in the present, the present is kept in the dependent clause
The imparfait marks the shift into indirect speech, not a habitual past meaning

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated condition; the second distinguishes this shift from the imparfait's aspectual use.

patches.entity_key: Past participle agreement with preceding direct object (que)
value: No agreement when the direct object follows the verb
No agreement with en or with indirect object pronouns
Agreement is with the direct object, not with the subject

evidence.notes: First two entries are standard counterparts to the agreement rule; the third is the stated agreement target.

patches.entity_key: Pendant vs pour for past duration
value: pendant may be omitted entirely (Il a habité cinq ans à Londres)
pour is never used for duration in the past

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated transformation; the second is the stated trap.

value: The affirmative takes the indicative, not the subjunctive
In the negative and interrogative the subjunctive is optional and signals greater uncertainty

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated trap; the optional nature of the subjunctive comes from the stated restriction.

patches.entity_key: Placement of short adverbs in passé composé
value: The adverb goes between the auxiliary and the past participle, not after the participle
Longer adverbs and time expressions stand outside the auxiliary + participle block

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated word order and trap; the longer-adverb contrast is standard usage.
